lines.text: But dearest—Did you not understand that I understood?
lines.note: Early proof that Elizabeth already reads Robert’s words deeply.

lines.text: So my reverie was broken in the middle—but being better tempered, rather, than Flush, or having larger resources, I did not growl, but took your latest letter out instead, which lasted for the whole remainder of the time.
lines.note: A tiny private scene: Flush at the window while she reads Robert’s letter.

lines.text: I thought once that the capacity of happiness was destroyed in me, but you have made it over again,—God has permitted you!
lines.note: Elizabeth’s happiness is remade by him after long despair.
Their shared word for the life-changing step they are taking.

lines.text: ‘Comfort me with apples, for I am sick of love!’
lines.note: Robert’s homely apple parable about not delaying their happiness.

lines.text: It seems to me that you and I are at one upon the whole question,—only that I am your Flush, and he is mine.
lines.note: Elizabeth turns the Flush argument into a tender mirror of their own bond.

lines.text: Come back safe, but without Flush—I am to have him to-night though.
lines.note: Her affectionate command that he come back safe, even without Flush.

lines.text: And smiling to myself I was, both last night and this morning, at your phrase about the ‘business’ to be talked by the ‘grave man and woman’; understanding your precaution against all unlawful jesting!—jesters forbidden in the protocol!
lines.note: Elizabeth smiles at Robert’s grave ‘business’ talk while jesters are forbidden.

lines.text: For Flush, I did your commission, kissing the top of his head: then I took the kiss back again because it seemed too good for him just now.
lines.note: Flush becomes a playful go-between for their kisses.

lines.text: Ever dearest, I write a word that you may read it and know how all is safe so far, and that I am not slain downright with the day—oh, such a day!
lines.note: The exhausted, breathless morning after the wedding.

lines.text: All that I am, I owe you—if I enjoy anything now and henceforth, it is through you.
lines.note: Elizabeth names him as the source of her renewed life.

lines.text: You take my words from me—I ‘exult’ in the irrevocability of this precious bestowal of yourself on me—come what will my life has borne flower and fruit—it is a glorious, successful, felicitous life, I thank God and you.
lines.note: Robert exults in the irrevocable gift of herself.

lines.text: And forgive the inveterate jesting, which jests with eyes full of tears.
lines.note: Jesting through tears at the edge of their new life.

lines.text: Is this my last letter to you, ever dearest?
lines.note: Her last letter before they leave England together.
